caption_fb: One of the biggest money-wasters for small businesses is sending paid ad traffic straight to their homepage. When someone clicks an ad for a specific service or offer, they expect to land directly on a page dedicated to that exact offer. If they have to search through navigation menus to find it, they just hit the back button and you lose the lead. If you want me to check if your site has these disconnects, drop me a DM with the word AUDIT and I'll record a quick video review for you.
caption_li:
Most small business websites do not have a traffic problem—they have a conversion disconnect.

When a prospective customer clicks an ad or search link, they expect immediate context. Directing targeted traffic to a generic homepage forces visitors to hunt for information, causing steep drop-off rates.

To protect your marketing spend:
1. Direct ad campaigns to dedicated single-offer landing pages.
2. Ensure top-performing articles end with a clear, direct call to action.

Send me a DM with 'AUDIT' if you would like a brief video review identifying potential drop-off points on your current website.

slides.title: Your website is leaking money from paid ad clicks.
slides.body: If your website messaging doesn't instantly match the exact offer in your ad or social post, visitors leave in seconds. Here are two costly mistakes you can fix today.

slides.title: Stop sending paid ad traffic to your homepage.
slides.body: If an ad promises '20% off roof repairs' but lands on a generic homepage, visitors won't hunt for the offer. They hit back. Send ad clicks to a page matching that specific offer.

slides.title: Blog readers leave when pages lack clear next steps.
slides.body: People finding your site through Google get their answer and immediately close the tab. If your articles and service pages don't end with a direct booking action, that organic traffic is lost.

slides.title: Let me find your website's hidden drop-off points.
slides.body: DM me the word AUDIT. I will record a free 5-minute video teardown showing where your site loses paying customers, and the exact changes needed to fix it.
